draft.title: Planning for population growth
card: When a city's population grows, it needs more of everything. Governments plan ahead so that the city can cope with extra people.
Plans usually cover four things: new housing, transport such as roads, trains and buses, services such as schools and hospitals, and green space such as parks.
A sustainable city meets the needs of people today without harming the environment or the needs of people in the future.
A liveable city is a good place to live. It has affordable homes, easy travel, local services and open space. Planners aim for both.
draft.remember: Planners match housing, transport, services and green space to growth, so cities stay sustainable and liveable.

a.q: Why do governments plan for growth in a city's population?
opts: So the city can meet the needs of extra people
So the city stops attracting new residents
So the city can move its jobs to the countryside
So the city can avoid building any new homes
a.why: Extra people need homes, transport, services and green space, so governments plan ahead to provide them. Planning does not aim to stop people arriving, because it is about coping with growth.
a.clue: Think about what extra people need.

b.q: A council on the outskirts of Perth expects thousands of new residents. It plans new suburbs with a train line, a hospital and several parks. Which plan for growth does the park show?
opts: Green space
Housing
Transport
Services
b.why: Parks are open areas for recreation, so they are green space. A train line is transport and a hospital is a service. The council is also planning new suburbs for housing.
b.clue: Parks are open areas, not buildings or travel routes.

a.best: So the city can meet the needs of extra people

problems.detail: The remember line says planning makes cities 'stay sustainable and liveable', as if this is a sure result. The card only says planners 'aim for both'. Reword it as an aim, for example 'so cities can be sustainable and liveable'.

The question asks about 'the park', but the scenario mentions 'several parks'. 'Which plan for growth does the park show?' is also awkward. Something like 'Which part of the plan are the parks?' would be clearer.
